_meta.note: Every leaf is {value, unit, source, estimate}. All values are placeholder estimates until the research teammate supplies sources. Replace value+source and set estimate:false.

activeHours.source: Estimate: campus activity from breakfast to late evening (hostel and canteen waste peaks around 8–10, 12–14 and 19–21); no campus-specific timing data

dailyNoise.source: Estimate: ±15% day-to-day variation in generation (attendance, events, weather); no campus logs yet — MRF weigh logs would replace this

pet_bottles.source: Estimate: bottle body PET (~90%), caps and rings PP (~8%), labels and other (~2%) by mass

hdpe.source: Estimate: HDPE containers (~85%) with PP caps (~10%) and labels/other (~5%) by mass

pp.source: Estimate: PP cups/containers (~85%) with film lids, straws and other (~15%) by mass

mixed.source: CPCB SOP for plastic waste characterisation (pwm.cpcb.gov.in/uploads/content_manager/80.pdf): Indian cities PET 14%, HDPE 11.7%, PP 15.6%; LDPE film 28.3% + multilayer 22.2% + PS 4.9% + PVC 3.2% counted as "mixed"

food_contaminated.source: Estimate: canteen plastic dominated by films, multilayer packets and cups (~60%); PP cups/containers ~25%

baseFraction.source: Estimate, tuned with singleBinCrossContamination to the 30–50% (mixed bins) / 10–20% (segregated) soiled range

singleBinCrossContamination.unit: added fraction (absolute) in single mixed bins
singleBinCrossContamination.source: Estimate: puts unsegregated plastic at ~35–40% too soiled to recycle and segregated at ~15–20% (published MRF reject rates 10–30%, e.g. PMC8931185)

segregatedCompliance.unit: fraction of users who segregate correctly
segregatedCompliance.source: Thapar case study "From theory to practice" (pdfs/) p18: "90% segregation at source achieved"

sideWasteContaminated.unit: fraction of non-lost overflow counted contaminated
sideWasteContaminated.source: Estimate: waste left beside an overflowing bin is soiled by ground contact and food waste, so all of it counts as contaminated

lossFraction.unit: fraction of overflow that becomes litter
lossFraction.source: Estimate (no published Indian figure): 10–30% of overflowing waste is scattered, blown or pulled out by animals

defaultCapacityL.source: Common 120 L wheeled bin (IndiaMART listings); default for newly added nodes

bulkDensityKgPerL.source: Estimate: loose uncompacted plastic ~15–60 kg/m³ (PET bottles 15–30 kg/m³); food-contaminated higher due to wet residue. No credible Indian source found

sizingHeadroom.unit: fraction of spare capacity to keep at pickup when sizing bins
sizingHeadroom.source: Project decision: smallest bin that fits expected fill + headroom

methods.source: Manual throughput: Thapar case study "From theory to practice" (pdfs/) p16–17, MRF sorts 1.5–1.75 t/day dry waste by hand with 21 workers; plastic ≈20% of recycled tonnage (DOC1 p4) → ~350 kg/day plastic capacity. Float-tank and NIR capacities, and all accuracy/loss values, are estimates

contaminatedToChemicalFraction.unit: fraction of removed contaminated mass suitable for chemical recycling
contaminatedToChemicalFraction.source: Estimate: half of the contaminated plastic is fit for chemical recycling / co-processing; Thapar sends MRF rejects to an authorised co-processing vendor (case study p16), so this may be higher in practice

detourFactor.source: Estimate: road distance ≈ 1.3 × straight-line distance on a gridded campus road network (typical urban circuity 1.2–1.4)

truckSpeedKmh.source: Estimate: e-loader on narrow campus roads (8–12 km/h)

stopMinutes.source: Estimate: 1–3 min per bin stop for a crew emptying wheeled bins

defaultMetresPerPixel.source: Google Maps zoom 17 at 30.354°N, captured at 2x pixel density (Web Mercator: 156543.03 × cos(lat) / 2^17 / 2); matches the 100 m scale bar within 2%

transportPerKm.source: Estimate for a battery e-loader (IndiaMART ₹85k, 500 kg): electricity + maintenance ₹2–4/km plus driver time at ~₹440/day and 10 km/h

binPerDay.unit: INR per bin per day by capacity in L (single bin; amortised)
binPerDay.source: IndiaMART list prices (120–240 L wheeled HDPE ₹1,450–3,650; 660 L ₹18,500; 60 L ~₹650 est.) amortised over an estimated 5–8 year life

sortingPerDay.source: Manual: 21 workers × ~₹440/day (Punjab unskilled minimum wage, w.e.f. 01.03.2025) × plastic share of MRF mass (~14%) + baler amortised (~₹3.5 lakh / 7 y). Float tank and NIR add estimated equipment and running costs

segregatedBinMultiplier.unit: × bin cost for a segregated set
segregatedBinMultiplier.source: Estimate: a labelled segregated set (wet/dry/hazardous, as at Thapar) costs about 1.6× a single bin of the same plastic capacity

balePricePerKg.unit: INR per kg of correctly sorted resin (sold to recyclers)
balePricePerKg.source: Indian dealer bale prices Oct 2026, set conservatively below asking prices: PET baled ₹44–50/kg city rates (scrapc.com), ₹35–55 (IndiaMART); HDPE ₹55–71 (scrapo.com, IndiaMART); PP ₹58 (scrapo.com). Only correctly sorted resin earns (bale grading by target-resin fraction, NAPCOR)

co2eAvoidedKgPerKg.unit: kg CO2e avoided per kg recycled
co2eAvoidedKgPerKg.source: US EPA WARM, recycling vs landfill (PET −1.04/+0.02, HDPE −0.76, PP −0.79 MTCO2E per short ton), converted per kg; US model, Indian grid differs
